newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds nearly match Treasuries' gains.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds nearly match Treasuries' gains.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities climbed higher on Wednesday, rising as much as 13/32 in discount coupons by late afternoon.
Discount coupon mortgage-backeds performed on par with their Treasury counterparts the day after the Federal Reserve made no change in short-term interest rates.
"Everyone was saying the knee-jerk reaction after the Fed didn't do anything would be a steepening (of the yield curve), because people would be concerned about inflation," said a trader.

Since the Fed is not expected to move inter-meeting, especially with the upcoming Presidential election, spread products look more attractive, he said. "Everyone bought the short-end of (the Yield curve) yesterday, now they are moving their way out."
Late on Wednesday, Ginne Mae 30-year 8.0 percent pass-throughs were up 7/32 at 100-30/32, yielding 120 basis points over 10-year Treasuries. The 10-year note had climbed 14/32 to yield 6.69 percent.
